In ripgrep, -r is --replace, and a clustered flag string starting with r (for example -riln) parses as --replace with the remaining letters as its argument, silently rewriting every match in the output instead of applying the intended flags. Spell flags separately (-i -l -n; ripgrep is already recursive). When replacement output is genuinely intended, use the explicit long form --replace=<text>, which this block does not match.

preToolUse.description: Block shell commands that destroy history, bypass safety gates, overwrite live working-tree edits, discard stashed work, or stage by wildcard. Each entry carries a `concept` (the pattern family it is a fingerprint of), a `citation` (the doctrinal anchor), and a `reappraisal` (the positive direction the firing signals) so the deny message TEACHES: it names a concept to reappraise and steers the agent away from reaching for a sibling destructive command, rather than only refusing (PDR-044 §Innate immunity, as amended; the doctrine that an enforcement surface must carry the advisory-response content, not only a refusal). The concepts: `history-destruction` (`git push --force` / `-f`, `git rebase -i`); `gate-bypass` (`git --no-verify`, `git --no-gpg-sign`); `worktree-destruction` (`git reset --hard`, `git clean -fd`, checkout/restore variants — these silently throw away in-flight edits, including peer-agent edits in parallel sessions, and `git fsck --lost-found` cannot recover them); `stash-discard` (`git stash drop` / `clear`); `wildcard-staging` (`git add -A` / `--all` / `.`, blocked under the explicit-pathspec discipline so a commit cannot accidentally bundle parallel-thread or unrelated work); `host-dos-unbounded-load` / `host-dos-forkbomb` (inline busy-loops, fork bombs, load tools — the host is a shared substrate and unbounded load is a denial of service against the owner and every session; see `.agent/rules/no-unbounded-host-load.md`); `silent-output-mangling` (ripgrep's short replace flag — a clustered flag string starting with r parses as replace-with-remainder and silently rewrites match output; spell flags separately, or use the explicit long form when replacement is genuinely intended); `filesystem-destruction` (`rm -rf` / `rm -fr`, with the forced worktree removal under `worktree-destruction` — nothing in the estate is removed by force, and a forced removal that seems necessary is a routed request to the Director, never a prompt for an absent owner; see `.agent/rules/unattended-seats-never-prompt.md`). We never use git to remove work; forward-going filesystem changes only. Entries may be bare strings (legacy) or objects; `concept` and `reappraisal` are optional at load time so a missing value never fails the guard closed (which would brick the worktree on a stale-dist/new-policy mismatch — a stale Bash guard blocks every command including the rebuild), and the `validate-policy-reappraisal` repo validator enforces their presence on object entries at commit-time. See `.agent/rules/never-use-git-to-remove-work.md`, `.agent/rules/no-verify-requires-fresh-authorisation.md`, and `.agent/rules/stage-by-explicit-pathspec.md`.

scoped_blocks.citation: principles.md §No machine-local paths; .agent/directives/privacy.md §Machine-local paths; no PII (a user-home absolute path leaks a username)
scoped_blocks.reappraisal: Use a repo-root-relative path for in-repo targets, or a platform-provided variable / tilde form (~/...) for per-user surfaces. A user-home or machine-temp absolute path resolves only on one machine and often leaks a username (PII). Portable system paths (/usr/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin) are fine; placeholder forms (/Users/<user>/) are fine.

preToolUseContent.description: Block agents from writing into Edit/Write content. Two surfaces: (blocked_patterns) the owner-approval marker, path-agnostic, which only the project owner may author; (scoped_blocks) path-scoped doctrine block GROUPS per PDR-044 §Innate immunity. Each group gathers the surface patterns for one concept and carries the doctrinal `citation` PLUS a `reappraisal` — the positive direction the firing signals — so a block teaches the agent to step back and re-assess the concept rather than to reword around the wall (PDR-044 §Innate immunity, as amended; the doctrine that an enforcement surface must carry the advisory-response content, not only a refusal). `kind` and the `excludes_*` options are group-level: every pattern in a group shares them. The six concepts: (literal) `expediency-hedging` — language that means 'I know the rule applies, but this situation is special' rejected on doctrine surfaces (PDRs, plans, ADRs, governance), with doctrine-defining surfaces excluded so principles.md, distilled.md, PDR-043/044/047 may catalogue the words they forbid; (literal) `acceptance-euphemism` — the owner-graduated acceptance-shaped euphemisms (labels that dress a known defect as handled without a routed fix or ratified policy), scoped to operational records (.agent/memory/operational/, .agent/reports/) in addition to doctrine surfaces because the graduating instances lived in continuity records, with the napkin out of scope as the first-capture observation buffer and no-hedging-vocabulary.md excluded as the cataloguing home; (regex) `sha-in-permanent-doc` — 7- to 40-character hex tokens with at least one a-f character on portable-permanent-doc paths (practice-core, rules, memory/active/patterns, principles.md, testing-strategy.md; ADRs are repo-bound and out of scope per PDR-079), with fenced code blocks, inline-code spans, and `(historical reference)` marker lines excluded; (regex) `indefinite-deferral` — deferral-to-nowhere vocabulary (owner-directed 2026-06-10) rejected on doctrine and operational-memory surfaces: work is a live deliverable with named gates or it is removed by owner decision, never left in an unagreed holding state; word-boundary regex so substrings inside names (e.g. agent display names containing 'Sparking') never false-positive, with no-hedging-vocabulary.md excluded as the cataloguing home; (literal) `menu-framing` — owner-decision phrasings rejected on architectural surfaces so menu-shaped option-sets do not slip past the re-apply-first-question-at-elaboration-boundaries discipline (the rule file itself is excluded so it may catalogue the phrases it forbids); (regex) `machine-local-path` — user-home and machine-temp absolute paths blocked EVERYWHERE (owner-directed invariant: the repo MUST NOT contain machine-local paths, ever; a user-home path also leaks a username = PII), with the pattern-defining surfaces (important-state-not-in-temp-files.md, this policy file) excluded so they may name the patterns (the teaching homes — principles.md §No machine-local paths and privacy.md §Machine-local paths — carry the shapes defanged and need no exclusion); portable system paths and placeholder forms (slash-user-placeholder) are exempt by construction (the regex requires a concrete segment); the same invariant is enforced over all tracked files at pre-push and CI (a leg of `pnpm check`) by the `validate-no-machine-local-paths` repo-validator, which single-sources its pattern set from this block. `reappraisal` is enforced present at commit-time by the `validate-policy-reappraisal` repo validator; it is optional at load time so a missing value never fails the guard closed. PDR-044 names false positives as a design property of the innate layer.
